newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis - forex rates better reflect fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis - forex rates better reflect fundamentals.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Wednesday that currency rates since the dollar's recent rise better reflected economic fundamentals.

"The dollar today is above 5.50 francs, more than eight percent above its level in 1996 and more than 10 percent above that of 1995," he said, according to a text of a speech to the Senate Finance Committee on Thursday.

"It is worth emphasising that this rebalancing in exchange rates, more in line with economic fundamentals, was obtained in an orderly way, while maintaining the stability of the franc in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism," he said.
"Moreover, in Europe, there has been a rebalancing in exchange rates with the rise in the pound sterling and the Italian lira," he added.
He later told reporters the rise in the dollar was a positive element for the French economy but declined to say whether he thought it had room to rise further.
He declined to say whether there was any dissent in the Group of Seven rich nations about the current level the dollar.
G7 finance ministers are due to meet in Berlin next month.
